text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Finance Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said fears that the size of Italy's public debt would block entry to Europe's single currency were unfounded.

* The centre-left Olive Tree governing coalition announced former anti-graft magistrate Antonio Di Pietro would run for the Senate. Di Pietro, who has previously served in the cabinet as public works minister as an independent, will stand in Florence.

* The Justice Commission of the Italian Senate has given the go-ahead to a bill which proposes to abolish prison life sentences. The bill, which must be passed by both houses of parliament, would set a maximum term of 32 years.
*Prime Minister Romano Prodi said the Italian economy would soon see an upturn in economic growth. (all)
* Prodi announced a packet of incentives on Wednesday aimed at boosting Italy's flagging building sector. (La Repubblica)
* The Milan bourse on Wednesday reached new highs with the historic Mib index at 13.926 points, breaking the previous index high set in May 1986.
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
